title.narrative: Vaccines, Therapeutics, and Diagnostics Manufacturing and Regulatory Strengthening Project

description.narrative: The Government has requested additional support of $338.13million from APVAX under the PIC. The project will have two phases: (i) Phase 1: fill and finish manufacturing of human vaccines, and (ii) Phase 2: full cycle development of selected vaccines. In the first 3 years, the project will support constructing a green, resilient, global enabling sustainability initiative-responsive manufacturing facility and commission equipment for manufacturing VTDs. By 2026, the project aims to start manufacturing fill and finish VTDs. By 2029, the project aims to start selected bulk substrate manufacturing and export of VTDs. The project will help strengthen DGDA's regulatory capacity from maturity level 2 to 3, essential to ensure safe and effective vaccine manufacturing and use. The project is aligned with the following impact: Pandemic preparedness increased, and the disease burden due to selected vaccine-preventable diseases in Bangladesh reduced. The project will have the subsequent outcome: availability of indigenously manufactured selected safe and efficacious VTDs in Bangladesh improved. The project will have the following outputs.Bangladesh has shown remarkable improvements in its health indicator outcomes. Between 2011 and 2022, the Under-5 mortality rate came down from 48 to 31 while the maternal mortality rate improved from 237 in 2012 to 123 as of 2020. The success of the expanded programme on immunization in Bangladesh is a significant factor contributing to declines in maternal and child mortality rates. However, the World Health Organization (WHO) Joint External Evaluation conducted in 2016 highlighted low pandemic preparedness indicators, including the availability of VTDs during public health emergencies. The prolonged COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated these challenges. The country reported 2,044,131 confirmed cases of COVID-19, with 29,469 deaths related to the disease. Bangladesh is at significant risk of infectious diseases as one of the most densely populated countries in the world. Bangladesh is one of the ten countries with the highest number of pneumonia cases and related deaths among children less than 5 years of age. Government health expenditure accounts for only 2.63% of the country's gross domestic product (ranking among the bottom 10 countries in the world).
